header: THE STEEL CARD: what steel costs, who makes how much, and how India and the world are doing. Five tabs. 1 "Prices": the retail prices of TMT bar, HR coil and CR coil in Mumbai, month by month, from the Ministry of Steel's monthly reports (the official benchmark), with the iron ore price beside them. 1b "DSP products": what the Durgapur Steel Plant makes to sell (its manuals: sizes, capacities) beside the Durgapur market's quotes for the same kind of steel (a trade-price site, dated, GST not included). The quotes are the market's, never DSP's or SAIL's own price: the tab says so. dsp.ts holds the figures and their sources. 2 "Companies": SAIL, Tata Steel, JSW Steel and Jindal Steel & Power quarter by quarter, from their own results: production, sales, EBITDA per tonne, and the results. 3 "SAIL & CPSEs": SAIL, RINL and NMDC Steel month by month (the Ministry's tables), SAIL against the same month a year earlier. 4 "India & world": India's crude steel, consumption and trade by year, and the biggest producers. There is NO price list of SAIL, Tata Steel or JSW to show: the mills sell at their own dealer rates, which differ by city, size and day, and none publishes them. The card says so, and I compare the companies by what they themselves report (the Companies tab). I fetch nothing here: the figures are reviewed files with their sources and dates (mos.ts, companies.ts); a figure that is not published is a dash.

symbols.name: SteelCard
symbols.sig: export function SteelCard({ initialTab = "prices" }: { initialTab?: SteelTab })
doc: `initialTab` is the tab the search line asked for: I open Prices for "steel prices", Companies for "steel companies" and the SAIL tab for "sail steel production".

behaviours: the card opens on the prices tab with five tabs: Prices, DSP products, Companies, SAIL & CPSEs, India & world
three product tiles with the September 2026 prices (TMT ₹65,750, HR coil ₹76,900, CR coil ₹89,670), Mumbai, GST included, with the month's change (+15.5%, +10.8%, +14.0%)
the card says plainly that no mill publishes a price list, so there is no brand-by-brand table, and points to the Companies tab
the figures table has the ten months, newest first, with each month's change; the source is the Ministry's report and is linked
the iron ore price and the flat-against-long premium are shown; the July report's slip is admitted
the chart (a trend chart of the month-ends) is drawn and has an accessible name
the DSP tab lists the seven products of the plant, each with its mill and manual page
six Durgapur market quotes are shown, GST not included (TMT 12 mm ₹45,200, channel ₹48,750, angle ₹44,500, billet ₹43,090, pig iron ₹41,500 and ₹46,500) with the 18% GST worked out beside each
the tab says plainly that these are market quotes, not DSP's or SAIL's selling prices, and that the size differs (TMT 12 mm against DSP's 20 and 25 mm)
joists and beams, and wheels and axles, show 'No market quote shown' with the reason, not a number
Durgapur is shown as the cheapest of the sixteen cities for TMT 12 mm, Goa 15.7% above
the plant's capacity is shown in MT (hot metal 2.40, crude steel 2.20, saleable steel 2.12) and the older figures of the plant manual are mentioned
the quotes are dated 13 Nov 2026; the 'old' warning appears exactly when they are more than seven days old (it is a clock test: it holds on any day)
every source is listed with its line and linked (ayronmart.com pages and the second billet report); the ticker's 45,500 is explained, not used

the ten-year hot metal chart: 2016-17 to 2025-26, four figures (2.52, 2.56, 2.57, 2.50 MT) and six years left empty with the reason, the best (2.57 MT in 2023-24) named, the capacity (2.40 and 2.45 MT) beside it
the empty years say why (below 2.52 MT, the best ever set in 2018-19; not above 2.52 MT; no 2025-26 figure) and the 2022-23 report's own 2.57 is admitted

the production section: four financial years, 2022-23 to 2025-26, with the figures SAIL states (hot metal 2.56, 2.57, 2.50; crude steel 2.29, 2.30, 2.26; saleable 2.18, 2.21, 2.15; finished 1.126) and dashes, not estimates, where it does not
semi-finished 2024-25 is 1.02 and marked 'worked out'; the changes on the year are shown (crude steel +0.4%, -1.7%; saleable +1.4%, -2.7%)

the three units of 2024-25 and the finished total are drawn as tiles: Bloom cum Round Caster 0.626, Medium Structural Mill 0.557, Merchant Mill 0.428, finished steel 1.126 with 0.141 beyond the two mills (worked out), in MT

the 2025-26 mix (54.7% longs, 45.3% semis) and the wheel, tyre and axle supply (42,024, 45,656, 47,200; +8.6%, +3.4%; 1,689 Vande Bharat wheels) are shown, with the note that they are items, not tonnes
the card says what the reports do not give (TMT, structurals, blooms, billets, wheels and axles in tonnes, nothing month by month), and every product has a 'Produced' line
the production sources are listed with their PDF pages and linked to SAIL's own documents (annual reports 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 and the Q4 FY26 presentation)
by-products (granulated slag, coal chemicals) are listed with no quote; no lakh and no 'Mt' on the tab
the companies tab compares four companies on production first, in order of size (JSW, Tata Steel, SAIL, Jindal Steel), each with its quarter, and a change on the year
the metric tabs are Production, Sales and EBITDA per tonne; Realisation is not offered because only SAIL states it
each company has its own quarter chart, and JSW's carries the note that BPSL left in March 2026
the results table has the four companies with their revenue, EBITDA and profit; Jindal Steel's revenue is a dash (it includes GST) and its bases are explained
the sources of every quarter are linked (Tata Steel's, SAIL's, JSW's, Jindal's) and the card says nothing is estimated
the dagger for a figure that comes from a report of a call is explained
JSW's change on the year is against the restated quarter (7.27 against 6.95 is +4.6%, 'same scope'), not against the 7.90 that included BPSL (that would read -8.0%)
the SAIL tab: September 2026 crude steel 1.492 MT (-0.9% on the year) and the year to date 9.605 against 9.505 (+1.1%), with no lakh tonnes shown
SAIL's realisation per tonne is charted, with the note that no other maker states a rupee figure; the three public-sector makers are compared on the latest month
the SAIL table has every month (nineteen) with the four figures; the source is the Ministry's report
the India tab: FY26 crude steel 170.2 MT (+11.8%), consumption 164.4 MT, April-September 85.1 MT (+2.9%), capacity 220.4 MT
the producers table has seven rows with India marked (164.9 in 2025, +10.4%) and the trade table seven years, net importer or net exporter in words
no tab has a question-mark badge or Bengali letters
the card uses only the text sizes that have a rule in the search window's stylesheet (xs to 4xl and 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, 17, 28 px) and no fixed leading
'steel prices', 'tmt price', 'hrc', 'steel rate today' open the prices tab
'steel companies', 'tata steel', 'jsw steel', 'steel comparison', 'jindal steel' open the companies tab
'sail steel production' and 'sail steel' open the SAIL tab; 'india steel production', 'steel production' and 'crude steel' the India tab
other lines are not this card: 'tata steel share price', 'steel plant', 'steel almirah price', 'sail' alone, 'sensex'
'dsp products', 'durgapur steel', 'billet price', 'tmt price durgapur', 'steel channel price' open the DSP tab
the Durgapur words do not take other cards: 'durgapur pin code', 'durgapur police station', 'durgapur' alone, 'dsp' alone
readLang reads the tab and falls back to prices
